items.title: Visual illusion reveals what today's AI vision is missing
items.excerpt: Our eyes do not always tell us exactly where things are—and that may be a feature of how biological vision works, rather than simply a flaw. A new study by York University researchers uses a common illusion to ask: If artificial intelligence is meant to see more like us, should it make some of the same systematic perceptual "mistakes"?
items.rationale: Perception-psychology study (York U.) testing whether AI vision models reproduce human illusion errors; fresh research result, cognitive-science angle.

items.title: Millions of years of evolution guide AI search for pollution-fighting enzymes
items.excerpt: Databases around the world contain information on millions upon millions of enzymes that have the potential to degrade pollutants like plastic. Scientists at Murdoch University's Bioplastics Innovation Hub are combining machine learning technology and biochemistry to identify which of these enzymes have the potential to break down plastic and other
items.rationale: Murdoch University ML + biochemistry screen for plastic-degrading enzymes; life-science/materials result with a clear environmental payoff.

items.title: Turning to AI for health answers may signal anxiety, depression among young adults
items.excerpt: Young adults who use generative artificial intelligence to ask health-related questions are more likely to screen positive for clinically significant anxiety and depression than those who do not use AI for health issues, according to a new study led by University of Florida researcher Yusen Zhai.
items.rationale: University of Florida clinical-psychology study linking generative-AI health queries to anxiety/depression screens; empirical data rather than opinion.

items.title: New tool lets users repair AI-generated 3D models, then fabricate them just the way they want
items.excerpt: The InstructMesh generative AI tool helps users 3D print working, real-world items with ease by understanding how designs should look and which edits users truly want. You can prompt the system to produce a 3D model, then ask it to edit specific parts.
items.rationale: MIT CSAIL research system (InstructMesh) where generative AI is the core result: part-level editing of AI-made 3D meshes into fabricable objects; adds an engineering/fabrication field and a fifth distinct outlet.

items.title: Introducing Quine: An AI research system designed for the complexity of biology
items.excerpt: Biology doesn't operate in silos, and neither should the AI representation of it. Quine is an early-stage research effort to create a multimodal world model of biology.
